judges.rationale:
The visible evidence supports the core shortage facts. E2 shows DS-2023-0205, Methotrexate Sodium, Injection 25mg/mL, NDC 43598-0025-10, status Current, posted 2023-08-05, revised 2024-01-17, reason Quality: cGMP Issue, related application ANDA065680. SYS supports the as-of date, the 21-of-150 linkage coverage, and the default interpretations. The 2024-01-17 revision is about 21 months before the as-of date, so the staleness caveat is also correct.

Much of the rest cannot be checked against the evidence provided. The evidence is cut off partway through E3, and E4 and E5 are not shown. These claims have no visible support:
- sponsor "Hospira Inc" on ANDA065680
- FEI 3005678901 and its format check
- the Rocky Mount facility
- the last inspection ending 2024-05-21 (FY2024), with 1 inspection and 0 OAI
- "The record has never changed status"
- "Both were checked, and both give the same single record"
- "Three independently written queries returned the same result". SYS does not mention this, and it reads as an invented verification claim.
- "The details of the record were confirmed with certified tools".

Under a strict standard, claims that the available evidence does not support count as failures. E1 only shows that "Hospira" resolves to the firm name "Hospira Inc". It does not link that firm to this shortage.

The answer has an explicit "Interpretation applied" section. It names the ambiguous phrase ("Manufacturer / tied to Hospira") and states the reading it used as the default: "the application sponsor is Hospira." It gives the alternate, "the facility operator is Hospira." It says the alternate gives the same result: "Both were checked, and both give the same single record." This claim is backed by E4, which shows Hospira Inc as both sponsor and facility operator for ANDA065680, so the two readings can't differ for this record. It also covers the "in shortage" status ambiguity. It says the one record is Current, so "the alternate (Current or Discontinued) gives the same result." The search also ran across all statuses. Weaknesses: (1) E3 matched sponsor OR operator in one query. The "both checked separately" wording is therefore somewhat stronger than the visible evidence shows, though E4 supports the outcome. (2) The "Currently" and "How many drugs" items are not in the question, so they add padding. (3) Other possible readings of "tied to" are not mentioned, such as NDC labeler code. These are minor, since the main ambiguity is named, resolved and shown to give the same result.
